# The Lights That Obey Their Maker

## Scripture

*"He made the moon to mark the seasons, and the sun knows when to go down."* — Psalm 104:19

## Reflection

Every autumn, something quiet and precise happens overhead. The constellation Orion climbs back into the evening sky, rising earlier each night like a faithful servant returning to his post. The Pleiades appear, the nights stretch longer, and the whole sky shifts with a punctuality no clockmaker could improve. The psalmist noticed this long before telescopes existed: the sun *knows* when to go down. The moon *marks* the seasons. Creation keeps its appointments.

We are not always so faithful. We oversleep. We wander. We let seasons slip past without noticing. Yet God's celestial clock never stutters — and that steadiness is a gift. When life feels aimless, the autumn sky preaches a sermon without a single word: *God is not chaotic. He is not forgetful. He is not late.*

There is a rhythm built into creation, and built into your life too — seasons of labor and rest, planting and harvest, waiting and arriving. The God who tells the sun when to set also holds your unfolding days. You do not have to rush the sky, and you do not have to rush your own soul. The One who keeps the stars on schedule will keep you.

## Prayer

Father, thank You for the faithful rhythm of the heavens. When my own seasons feel uncertain, remind me that You are never off schedule. Teach me to trust Your timing and to rest in Your steady hand. Amen.
